newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs back off highs in late trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs back off highs in late trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures backed off in late Friday trade as Japanese government bond (JGB) futures took a breather after surging to a new high.
"It was just some profit-taking and position adjustment in line with the fall in JGBs," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
He said December JGBs were taken to a new high of 125.71 on talk of buying of cash bonds by Japanese agricultural cooperatives. They ended at 125.53 against a previous 125.44.
Market consensus forecasts call for a 212,000 rise in non-farm payrolls for October and 0.4 percent rise in average hourly earnings.

"Anything between 150,000 and 175,000 will be quite positive especially given last month's drop of 40,000," said a trader with a U.S. house. "The general picture we're seeing now is that inflation isn't too much of a worry."
The dealer at the Japanese institution said players were unlikely to panic even if the payrolls figure exceeded 200,000.
He said they looked excessively overbought and could correct downwards to 123.50, but players were reluctant to sell them off given their recent climb to dizzying new highs on a daily basis.
June Euroyen stood at 99.27 in late trade against its IMM close at 99.29. September was at 99.13 against 99.14. Volume for both months was under 12,000 lots.
Dealers said comments by a Japanese Economic Planning Agency official that the economic recovery was becoming firmer had little impact.
Eurodollar futures saw some buying interest ahead of the closely watched U.S. non-farm payrolls report, due at 1230 GMT.
"Everyone is not expecting a rate hike this year. So even if a strong number comes in, they will wait for more data to confirm (a trend)," he said.
March Eurodollars finished at 94.46 against their IMM close at 94.44.
